sector: Healthcare Services (NZ Primary Care / Aged Residential Care Medical Services)
overview: Third Age Health Services Limited is New Zealand's leading dedicated provider of managed primary medical services to the aged residential care (ARC) sector, delivering GP and Nurse Practitioner-led care to residents in rest homes, private hospitals, secure dementia units and retirement villages nationwide, alongside a smaller general practice business serving the wider community in Auckland and Hawke's Bay. Now 15 years old, TAH operates as a national platform built through organic facility wins and disciplined bolt-on acquisitions of founder-owned ARC medical practices. Revenue is funded predominantly through NZ Government primary care capitation (via PHOs) and fee-for-service consultations, and the company operates exclusively within New Zealand.

business_model.summary: TAH generates revenue through two segments: ARC Medical Services (FY26 revenue $14.921M, +27% YoY, ~66% of total) and Community General Practice ($7.567M, +3.2% YoY, ~34% of total). Revenue is largely recurring — monthly capitation payments from PHOs based on enrolled-patient counts and demographics, supplemented by per-visit consultation fees. The model is asset-light (clinicians deliver care within client-owned ARC facilities or leased GP clinic premises under service contracts), giving high operating leverage as the patient base scales. TAH grows the ARC segment through bolt-on acquisition of small, founder-owned ARC medical practices at modest multiples, integrated using its 'Third Age Way of Working' (TAWoW) Kaizen-based operating system, and has explicitly stopped acquiring further Community GP practices after negative experience with small-practice economics (e.g. Belmont Medical Centre closure, FY26). The Q1 FY27 trading update (quarter to 30 June 2026) showed continued momentum: group revenue +20.9% YoY to $6.082M, ARC-related revenue +33.2% YoY to $4.223M, and the ARC footprint reaching 124 facilities (+37.8% YoY).

revenue_streams.name: Community General Practice (capitation + consultation)
revenue_streams.trend: stable/low-growth, patient attrition offset by pricing

business_model.customer_type: B2B (ARC facility operators as primary clients; NZ Government / Health NZ / PHOs as primary funder; individual ARC residents and GP patients as end-users)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand. National ARC footprint including Auckland, Wellington/Lower North Island, Northland, Canterbury (via ARC Health, Sept 2025) and Bay of Plenty (via Cicada Health, Sept 2025), now spanning 124 ARC facilities (Q1 FY27); Community GP concentrated in Auckland (Devonport, Ponsonby) and Hawke's Bay. No foreign operations or currency exposure.

main_competitors: Independent/owner-operator GPs and small regional GP networks servicing ARC facilities on an ad hoc basis
Large integrated aged-care operators (Ryman Healthcare, Bupa NZ, Summerset, Oceania Healthcare, Metlifecare, Arvida) — indirect competition where facilities manage medical services in-house
Locum GP/NP staffing agencies (compete for scarce clinician supply rather than for facility contracts)
General practice owner-operators and PHOs more broadly, for Community GP patient enrolments
competitive_position.market_position: Largest dedicated national provider of managed primary medical care to ARC facilities in New Zealand, with an estimated ~17-18% share of the ARC medical services market and a stated medium-term target of 20%. No competitor operates at equivalent national scale in this specific niche. Named sole preferred medical services partner by the Aged Care Association New Zealand (Sept 2025); ARC footprint continued to expand through Q1 FY27 (124 facilities, +37.8% YoY, including the Sept-2025 ARC Health/Cicada Health acquisitions and continued organic facility wins).

moat_factors.description: National footprint across ARC facilities, expanded into Canterbury and Bay of Plenty via the FY26 ARC Health and Cicada Health acquisitions and now spanning 124 facilities as of Q1 FY27, gives TAH a clinician network, rostering infrastructure, and management system that small-scale competitors cannot easily replicate. Facility relationships tend to be sticky given the operational burden of switching medical service providers.

Digital Clinical Portal live in 30+ facilities (from 13 at March 2025), supporting 900+ scheduled clinical rounds; Phase 2/3 development underway. Paired with TAH's independently-audited 'Residential Care Medical Service Provider Standard' (Elder Care Standards), this creates differentiation versus the fragmented visiting-clinician norm and could become a de facto sector benchmark.

moat_factors.factor: PHO contract relationships and regulatory/administrative complexity
moat_factors.description: Capitation revenue flows via PHO agreements recognised as intangible assets on acquisition. Navigating ARC-specific enrolment rules and maintaining PHO relationships is a meaningful barrier for new entrants. Sole preferred partner status with the Aged Care Association New Zealand reinforces sector standing and provides a platform for sector-level advocacy.

NP Development Programme (first graduates in the pipeline) and structured GP training pathways provide a partially self-sustaining talent funnel in an otherwise severely undersupplied labour market — a structural differentiator smaller operators cannot fund.

The 'Third Age Way of Working' provides a standardised, low-cost playbook for onboarding new facilities and integrating acquisitions, difficult for competitors to replicate quickly and supportive of margin durability even through a period of deliberate margin compression to protect service quality (FY26).

weaknesses: Small absolute scale (~NZ$22.5M FY26 revenue, ~NZ$44-49M market cap through most of 2026, though price reporting remains highly dispersed/stale across data providers) limits negotiating leverage with Health NZ/PHOs and constrains access to low-cost capital

Community GP segment (~34% of revenue) continues to lose enrolled patients — down 4.8% in FY26 (third consecutive year of decline) and organic enrolments fell a further 6.7% YoY in Q1 FY27, even as total enrolled patients (including acquisitions) rose 2.1% to 26,308
Dependent on an acutely thin clinician labour market — management states ARC growth is 'constrained' by clinical workforce availability, not by demand

FY26 letter to shareholders disclosed the forced closure of the small Belmont Medical Centre practice after safety incidents with disruptive patients, illustrating operational fragility of small acquired practices and informing management's decision to stop acquiring further Community GP practices
Minority-owned subsidiaries (Hub Aged Care 70%, ARC Health 80%, Cicada Health 70%, and other GP entities) create governance complexity and NCI dilution of parent earnings

NZX micro-cap illiquidity; share price swung across a wide range through FY26 and into FY27 (data providers show inconsistent, likely stale, quotes spanning roughly NZ$1.6 to NZ$7+ depending on snapshot date), consistent with the Chairman's prior statement that this volatility does not reflect a realistic assessment of intrinsic value in either direction

Key leadership transition risk: Niomi Fleming, ARC business General Manager, stepped down for health reasons at end of July 2026, shortly after being confirmed in the permanent GM role; successor arrangements not yet independently confirmed in public sources reviewed

growth_drivers: NZ demographic tailwind: population aged 65+ was ~16.6% of NZ in 2023 (up from 12.3% in 2006) and is projected to reach ~28% by 2073; the 65+ dependency ratio is projected to rise from ~25 per 100 working-age people (2024) to 43-57 per 100 by 2078. This is a multi-decade, non-cyclical structural demand driver for ARC medical services.

ARC market share expansion: TAH targets ~20% of the ARC medical services market (from an estimated ~17-18% currently), via a mix of organic facility wins (management notes ongoing inbound interest from ARC facilities, constrained mainly by clinical workforce availability) and further bolt-on acquisitions. The ARC footprint reached 124 facilities by Q1 FY27 (+37.8% YoY), with organic ARC enrolled-patient growth of 2.5% YoY in the quarter.

Bolt-on acquisitions at attractive multiples, ARC-focused: Hub Aged Care (April 2024, $742k, Wellington), ARC Health (Sept 2025, $1.10-1.12M, Canterbury), Cicada Health (Sept 2025, $0.86-0.875M, Bay of Plenty) — all immediately EBITDA-accretive with founders remaining as active co-owners. No new acquisitions have been announced since Sept 2025 as of this review (roughly 14 months), though management continues to describe an active pipeline. Chairman has explicitly stated the company will not allocate further capital to acquiring additional Community GP practices, sharpening capital allocation toward ARC and adjacent opportunities.

ARC capitation rate increases and reweighting — now CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED: the new demographically-reweighted capitation formula (incorporating age, sex, multimorbidity, rurality and socioeconomic deprivation) took effect from 1 July 2026 after 86% of GP practices voted in favour of Health NZ's 2026-27 funding package (per Health Minister Simeon Brown, June 2026). The package includes a 6.32% base capitation increase, a guaranteed minimum 4% increase per practice post-reweighting, and an additional $128.4M of government investment in primary care. This resolves what was previously an uncertain, pending policy item into a confirmed, implemented tailwind; the precise per-patient revenue benefit for TAH's older, higher-acuity ARC population should become observable in FY27 results (Q1 FY27's 33.2% YoY ARC revenue growth is an early positive data point, though it also reflects the ARC Health/Cicada Health acquisitions and facility-count growth, so the organic funding-formula effect is not yet cleanly isolated).

Digital Clinical Portal rollout: live in 30+ facilities as of H1 FY26 (from 13 at March 2025), supporting 900+ scheduled clinical rounds; Phase 2 in development, Phase 3 in planning. Reduces per-patient administrative cost, improves care quality metrics, and strengthens client retention.

AI and virtual care: AI transcription tools reducing clinician documentation burden; telehealth/virtual care solutions extending after-hours ARC coverage, effectively expanding clinician capacity without proportional headcount growth.

Elder Care Standards adoption: TAH's independently-assessed Residential Care Medical Service Provider Standard, if adopted more broadly across the sector or referenced in future regulation, would give TAH first-mover compliance advantage and enhanced client stickiness.

business.description: The large majority of TAH's revenue ultimately flows from Health New Zealand (Te Whatu Ora), either as capitation via PHOs or consultation fee schedules. The FY27 capitation package (6.32% base uplift, reweighted formula, effective 1 July 2026) was agreed and implemented, removing near-term funding-freeze risk, but TAH remains structurally a price-taker in the government-funded primary care system with limited negotiating leverage over the medium term. Cabinet has agreed to review capitation every five years (first review from 2028), which sets the next point of funding-policy uncertainty.

business.risk: Clinical workforce shortage and wage inflation
business.description: NZ faces a structural GP/NP shortage (over half of GPs aged 50+, a meaningful share of practices closed to new enrolments, a multi-year projected GP deficit). ARC growth is explicitly capacity-constrained by clinician availability per the FY26 letter to shareholders ('our primary operational risk remains the supply of clinical talent... failing to fill vacancies would directly lead to a loss of business'). Cost of services (predominantly clinician remuneration) rose to $11.4M in FY26 (~51% of revenue) from $9.18M (~48%) in FY25, and FY26 margin compression in the ARC segment was a deliberate trade-off to secure clinical coverage. No public data reviewed since August 2026 indicates this constraint has eased.

business.risk: Community GP segment structural decline and small-practice fragility
business.description: Community GP enrolled patients fell for a third consecutive year, down 4.8% to 19,383 in FY26, driven by doctor departures and unfilled vacancies (now filled). The Q1 FY27 trading update showed organic enrolled-patient population (ex-acquisitions) still declining 2.0% YoY overall, with general practice enrolments down 6.7% YoY, indicating the Community GP attrition trend has not yet stabilised as of the most recent available data point. The FY26 letter disclosed TAH was forced to close its small Belmont Medical Centre site after safety incidents — a 'clear reminder of the operational fragility of acquiring very small practices' — and management has explicitly ruled out further Community GP acquisitions.

Niomi Fleming, only recently confirmed as permanent General Manager of the ARC business (TAH's strongest-performing segment), stepped down for health reasons at the end of July 2026 as previously flagged. No independently confirmed successor appointment was found in public sources reviewed as of early November 2026. Executive Chairman John Fernandes (a hands-on capital allocator) and Founder/Director Bevan Walsh remain central to strategy and culture; the company's small management team increases disruption risk from any senior departure. Lucy Wu continues as Acting GM of Community GP leading its turnaround.

TAH completed four ARC acquisitions in roughly two years, each with founders retained as minority co-owners (70-80% TAH ownership). Deferred contingent consideration on ARC Health ($280k) and Cicada Health ($219k) fell due around September 2026; no public confirmation of settlement (payment, clawback, or dispute) was found in sources reviewed, so this remains an open item pending the next financial disclosure (H1 FY27 results). Rapid growth in subsidiary count adds integration complexity, and alignment with active founder-operators on strategy, compensation or eventual exit terms could create friction.

TAH issued a patient communications update in January 2026 relating to the MMH cybersecurity breach in late 2025 (MMH is a third-party patient portal used across NZ primary care). TAH patient data may have been compromised; no material financial impact has been disclosed, but reputational risk exists.

financial.risk: Small-cap illiquidity and volatile market pricing
financial.description: With roughly 9.95-10.9 million shares and a market cap in the roughly NZ$44-50M range for most of 2026, TAH is a micro-cap with thin trading volumes. The Chairman previously disclosed a ~3x intra-year trading range (NZ$2.50-$7.50) during FY26, which he described as an unrealistic assessment of intrinsic value at both ends; third-party data providers checked in this review show inconsistent and likely stale quotes spanning a similarly wide range into FY27, consistent with continuing illiquidity. This limits institutional participation, widens bid-ask spreads, and constrains TAH's ability to use equity as acquisition currency.

financial.risk: Bank debt and lease liabilities at floating/contracted rates
financial.description: As at March 2026, TAH carried $1.09M in bank loans (current + non-current) and $2.26M in lease liabilities, funded partly via a line of credit (drawn briefly for the ARC Health/Cicada Health acquisitions and promptly repaid). Total debt remains modest relative to FY26 EBITDA of $5.75M. Interest rate risk is limited but real; declining NZ OCR (from 2023-24 peak) is a modest tailwind for borrowing costs.

financial.risk: Intangible asset concentration and amortisation growth
financial.description: Intangible assets grew to $6.67M at March 2026 (from $4.77M at March 2025) as ARC Health and Cicada Health goodwill/PHO-agreement intangibles were recognised. Amortisation and depreciation rose to $1.07M in FY26 (from $841k in FY25), structurally reducing statutory NPAT relative to underlying NPATA as the acquisition portfolio grows. EastMed and other marginal CGUs carry limited goodwill headroom.

regulatory.risk: Health NZ funding reform and capitation reweighting
regulatory.description: DOWNGRADED from moderate: the new capitation formula (incorporating age, sex, multimorbidity, rurality, and socioeconomic deprivation) is now confirmed implemented from 1 July 2026, following an 86% GP-practice vote in favour of the package (6.32% base uplift, guaranteed minimum 4% per-practice increase, $128.4M additional government investment). This removes near-term policy-uncertainty risk; residual risk is now about the precise quantum of benefit to TAH's specific ARC patient mix, which will only be cleanly observable once FY27 results are reported, and about the first scheduled five-yearly review of the formula from 2028.

A government-convened advisory process on aged-care funding models has been underway, with potential implementation from 2027. Any shift toward bundled ARC-operator payments rather than direct GP capitation could fundamentally alter TAH's revenue model, though the stated government policy intent (reducing hospital pressure via stronger community/ARC care) is broadly supportive of TAH's role. No material update identified since August 2026.

Ongoing Health NZ structural reform has reduced the number of PHOs nationally. If TAH's PHO partners merge or consolidate, contract renegotiation could affect capitation rates or enrolment terms. No specific adverse developments were identified in the review period.

macro.description: DOWNGRADED from high: Health New Zealand agreed and funded a 2026-27 primary care package (6.32% base capitation uplift plus $128.4M additional investment), suggesting fiscal capacity to support primary care funding has not deteriorated further in the near term despite Health NZ's 2024 Commissioner-control structural deficit background. TAH's revenue per enrolled patient nonetheless remains entirely dependent on future government funding decisions; any subsequent capitation freeze or reduction would directly compress margins given TAH's limited pricing power.

macro.risk: NZ economic conditions affecting GP co-payments
macro.description: TAH's ARC business is largely insulated from the economic cycle (ARC residents are government-funded). The Community GP segment earns some fee-for-service co-payments that could soften in a downturn, but this is a modest share of total revenue.

execution.description: Enrolled GP patients have declined for three straight years and organic GP enrolments were still down 6.7% YoY in Q1 FY27, despite leadership changes (Lucy Wu as Acting GM) and process improvements that lifted segment profitability. Continued decline increases the risk of further site closures (as with Belmont) and goodwill impairment at marginal CGUs like EastMed.

In FY26 management evaluated (via term sheets that ultimately did not proceed) acquisitions outside healthcare in life-safety, compliance, and maintenance/repair/operations sectors. No new non-healthcare deal has been identified as completed or pending as of this review. Continued pursuit of adjacent-sector M&A introduces execution risk if management ventures into unfamiliar industries, even though discipline shown to date (walking away from term sheets that didn't meet return criteria) is a positive signal.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ aged-care demand is structurally growing on demographics: the 65+ share of population rose from 12.3% (2006) to 16.6% (2023) and is projected to reach ~28% by 2073, with the 65+ dependency ratio roughly doubling by 2078. ARC facility supply is constrained by land, construction costs and staffing, keeping occupancy high and demand for in-facility medical services growing in parallel. The primary care sector faces chronic structural underfunding (capitation formula unchanged since 2002 until now) but received its largest uplift in over a decade for FY26/FY27, with the demographically-reweighted formula now confirmed implemented from 1 July 2026 (86% GP-practice support, 6.32% base increase, $128.4M additional investment). GP/NP supply remains structurally short and is not expected to improve materially for 5-10 years.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Very low. ARC medical services are non-discretionary healthcare funded primarily by government capitation; Community GP services are partially fee-based (co-payments) but still predominantly government-funded. TAH's revenue has grown through COVID-19 and NZ's 2023-24 economic slowdown without interruption, and growth continued through Q1 FY27.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity — total debt (bank loans + leases) of roughly $3.3M at March 2026 relative to FY26 EBITDA of $5.75M. Indirect benefit from a declining NZ OCR (down from a 5.5% 2023-24 peak) reduces borrowing costs and supports continued acquisition financing.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: None. TAH operates exclusively in New Zealand; revenue, costs and capital structure are entirely NZD-denominated.
key_input_costs: GP and Nurse Practitioner remuneration (largest cost; cost of services rose to ~51% of revenue in FY26 from ~48% in FY25, reflecting deliberate investment in clinical coverage)
Technology and digital enablement (Digital Clinical Portal build-out)
Lease costs for GP clinic premises

recent_developments.event: REVIEW NOTE: No new acquisition, divestment, corporate action (takeover approach, capital raise, or delisting), or material regulatory shock was identified since the prior analysis (2026-08-01). The most significant confirmed development is implementation of the new primary-care capitation funding formula from 1 July 2026 (see below), which converts a previously pending policy item into a confirmed tailwind. TAH's H1 FY27 results (six months to 30 September 2026), expected around late October/early November 2026 based on the prior-year reporting calendar and pattern of late release, do not yet appear to have been published or indexed as of this review date; they should be checked at the next refresh as they will be the first clean read on FY27 margins and the capitation-reweighting revenue impact. The status of the ARC Health ($280k) and Cicada Health ($219k) deferred contingent consideration, which fell due around September 2026, could not be independently confirmed as settled, disputed, or adjusted from the public sources reviewed.

TAH released its Q1 FY27 (quarter to 30 June 2026) unaudited trading update: group revenue up 20.9% YoY to $6.082M (+3.8% on Q4 FY26), ARC-related revenue up 33.2% YoY to $4.223M, statutory NPAT up 33.1% YoY to $865k, and NPATA up 36.3% YoY to $1.025M. ARC services extended to 124 facilities (+37.8% YoY). Total enrolled patients (ARC + Community GP) rose 2.1% YoY to 26,308 including acquisitions, but the combined population excluding acquisitions declined 2.0% YoY — organic ARC enrolments grew 2.5% YoY while organic Community GP enrolments fell 6.7% YoY, indicating the GP segment's multi-year patient attrition has not yet stabilised. The board declared a Q1 FY27 interim dividend of 4.00 cents per share (fully imputed), unchanged from the fixed quarterly policy.

Health Minister Simeon Brown announced that 86% of GP practices voted in favour of Health NZ's 2026-27 primary care funding package, confirming implementation of the demographically-reweighted capitation formula (age, sex, multimorbidity, rurality, socioeconomic deprivation) effective 1 July 2026. The package includes a 6.32% base capitation rate increase, a guaranteed minimum 4% increase per practice after reweighting, and an additional NZ$128.4M of government investment in primary care — resolving prior uncertainty about whether and how the reform would proceed, and removing a previously 'pending' risk item for TAH's largely elderly, high-acuity ARC patient base. Cabinet separately agreed to review the capitation formula every five years, with the first review from 2028.

TAH released its audited FY26 Annual Report (year ended 31 March 2026): revenue $22.488M (+17.9% YoY), EBITDA $5.747M, underlying EBIT $5.291M (margin 23.5%, +1.1pp YoY), statutory NPAT $3.091M (+24.7%), underlying NPATA $3.634M (+25.9%), diluted EPS 28.38 cents (+24.8%), ROE 55.9% (TTM), ROCE 44.1% (TTM). ARC segment revenue grew 27% to $14.921M with 7,138 enrolled patients; Community GP revenue grew 3.2% to $7.567M but enrolled patients fell 4.8% to 19,383. Full-year dividend 16.00 cps (+8.8% YoY). The Chairman's letter disclosed the forced closure of the Belmont Medical Centre practice after safety incidents, confirmed the company will not acquire further Community GP practices, and disclosed that ARC business GM Niomi Fleming would step down for health reasons at end of July 2026.

TAH released preliminary unaudited FY26 full-year results broadly consistent with the subsequent audited figures, describing the FY27 operating backdrop as 'difficult' given ongoing workforce shortages and cost pressures.

TAH reported Q3 FY26 performance: quarterly NPAT of $818k, up 16.7% YoY. Board declared a Q3 FY26 interim dividend of 4.00 cents per share (fully imputed), consistent with the fixed quarterly dividend policy.

TAH issued a patient information update regarding the Manage My Health (MMH) cybersecurity breach that occurred in late 2025; MMH is a third-party patient portal used across NZ primary care. No material financial impact was disclosed.

TAH released H1 FY26 results (six months to 30 September 2025): revenue $10.653M (+13.2% YoY), NPAT $1.520M (+31.7% YoY), underlying NPATA $1.742M (+28.0% YoY). ARC enrolled patients 7,159 (including 1,684 from the ARC Health and Cicada Health acquisitions); organic ARC enrolled patients grew 3.7% YoY. GP enrolled patients 20,032 (-2.4% YoY). Digital Clinical Portal live in 30+ facilities, supporting 900+ scheduled clinical rounds.

TAH acquired 80% of ARC Health Limited (Canterbury, ~$1.10-1.12M total consideration) and 70% of Cicada Health Limited (Bay of Plenty/Tauranga, ~$0.86-0.875M total consideration), effective 1 September 2025, funded from cash and a brief line-of-credit drawdown (promptly repaid). Both were immediately EBITDA-accretive with founders remaining active co-owners. Deferred contingent consideration of $280k (ARC Health) and $218.75k (Cicada Health) fell due around September 2026 subject to performance conditions; settlement status not independently confirmed as of this review.

guidance.as_of: Q1 FY27 Trading Update (31 July 2026); FY26 Annual Report (26 June 2026)

items.target: No explicit numerical FY27 target disclosed; management continues to frame the operating backdrop as 'difficult' on workforce/cost grounds, though Q1 FY27 actuals (revenue +20.9%, NPAT +33.1%, NPATA +36.3% YoY) significantly outpaced that cautious framing
items.vs_prior: maintained cautious qualitative tone from the FY26 letter, but Q1 FY27 print was a positive surprise relative to that tone
items.notes: FY26 letter to shareholders: 'We expect the operating environment to remain difficult. Workforce shortages and cost pressures are a fact of life.' Q1 FY27 (quarter to 30 June 2026) nonetheless delivered 20.9% revenue growth and NPAT/NPATA growth of 33-36% YoY, aided by the ARC Health/Cicada Health acquisitions and ARC facility-count expansion to 124. No formal numeric FY27 revenue or earnings guidance has been issued.

items.target: 4.00 cents per share per quarter (16 cps annualised), fully imputed
items.period: FY26 and continuing into FY27 (Q1 FY27 interim dividend of 4.00 cps declared 31 July 2026, unchanged from Q1 FY26)
items.vs_prior: maintained at the fixed quarterly rate established for FY26
items.notes: Policy changed from a ~75%-of-NPAT payout ratio to a fixed quarterly cents-per-share amount from FY26, providing shareholders greater certainty while preserving flexibility to reinvest for growth. FY26 total dividend of 16.00 cps was up 8.8% on FY25's 14.71 cps; Q1 FY27 dividend held flat at 4.00 cps YoY.

items.target: ~20% of the NZ ARC population medium-term (originally framed as a 5-year target from FY24)
items.notes: Estimated at ~17-18% as of FY25/FY26, with the ARC facility count reaching 124 by Q1 FY27 (+37.8% YoY). Organic growth is constrained by clinical workforce availability rather than by facility demand; the newly-implemented capitation formula from July 2026 may lift funding per patient for TAH's higher-acuity population, though the clean organic effect is not yet separable from acquisition-driven growth in reported figures.

items.target: Continued bolt-on ARC acquisitions; explicit halt on further Community GP acquisitions; opportunistic evaluation of non-healthcare recurring-revenue businesses
items.vs_prior: maintained; no new acquisition announced since Sept 2025 as of this review (~14 months)
items.notes: Chairman's FY26 letter: searching for 'mission critical services or products, with recurring and predictable revenue, a demonstrated ability to generate free cash flow and earn returns on tangible capital in line with our expectations,' from founders 'planning for their own third age.' Deferred contingent consideration for ARC Health ($280k) and Cicada Health ($218.75k) fell due around September 2026 if performance conditions were met; settlement not independently confirmed in sources reviewed. No new M&A announced since.

guidance.management_commentary: FY26 Chairman's letter (John Fernandes, Executive Chairman): 'While the underlying demand for aged residential care and primary care continues to grow... the broader system is struggling to keep up... Our primary operational risk remains the supply of clinical talent... We expect the operating environment to remain difficult. Workforce shortages and cost pressures are a fact of life, and we are not expecting any near-term relief.' On valuation and capital allocation: 'Neither of these prices [NZ$2.50-$7.50 range during FY26] was a realistic assessment of per-share intrinsic value... our focus will always be on maximising the average annual rate of increase in intrinsic value per share.' No updated Chairman commentary has been identified since the Q1 FY27 trading update (31 July 2026), which pre-dates this review's cutoff by only one day and was already substantially reflected in the prior analysis; the H1 FY27 result (expected ~Oct/Nov 2026) will be the next material commentary checkpoint.

bull_case: Structural demographic tailwind is among the most powerful and certain long-duration growth drivers available on the NZX: NZ's 65+ population share is projected to nearly double by 2073, and the 85+ cohort (highest ARC utilisation) grows fastest of all. TAH is the only NZX-listed pure-play services provider (not a property owner like Ryman or Summerset) positioned to capture this trend directly.

The FY27 capitation funding package is now confirmed implemented (not merely proposed): 86% of GP practices voted in favour, delivering a 6.32% base capitation increase, a guaranteed minimum 4% per-practice increase, and $128.4M of additional government investment from 1 July 2026 — a funding tailwind largely outside TAH's control but now de-risked and directly beneficial to its economics, especially given TAH's older, higher-acuity ARC patient mix.

Momentum continued into FY27: the Q1 FY27 trading update showed group revenue +20.9% YoY, NPAT +33.1% YoY and NPATA +36.3% YoY, with ARC revenue up 33.2% YoY and the ARC footprint expanding to 124 facilities (+37.8% YoY) — a notably stronger print than management's own cautious 'difficult environment' framing implied.

Consolidation of a fragmented niche at attractive valuations, using a proven, repeatable playbook: Hub Aged Care, ARC Health and Cicada Health were each acquired at modest total consideration relative to the EBITDA/revenue contributed, immediately accretive, with founders retained as engaged co-owners. Management has shown capital discipline by walking away from non-healthcare term sheets that didn't meet return criteria.

High and resilient profitability with real operating leverage: FY26 underlying EBIT margin 23.5% (up from 22.4% in FY25), ROCE 44.1% and ROE 55.9% (TTM), despite deliberate margin compression in the ARC segment to secure clinical coverage. The business is asset-light, capital-light, and converts a high proportion of EBIT to free cash flow, supporting a fixed and growing quarterly dividend (16 cps annualised, +8.8% YoY, held flat into Q1 FY27).
bear_case: Growth appears to be re-accelerating (Q1 FY27 revenue +20.9%, NPAT +33%) even as management continues to guide cautiously to a 'difficult' operating environment — this disconnect could mean either genuine conservatism (upside optionality) or that one-off acquisition/capitation effects are flattering the headline numbers ahead of a later deceleration; the market cannot yet distinguish the two without the H1 FY27 result.

Community GP enrolled-patient decline has NOT stabilised: organic (ex-acquisition) enrolments were still down 2.0% YoY overall in Q1 FY27, with Community GP specifically down 6.7% YoY — a fourth consecutive period of attrition following the Belmont practice closure, and management's turnaround under Acting GM Lucy Wu remains unresolved.

The clinical workforce shortage is structural and, by management's own account, is the binding constraint on ARC growth — not demand. Cost of services rose to ~51% of revenue in FY26 (from ~48% in FY25) as TAH paid up to secure clinical coverage, and no evidence of easing has been found through Q1 FY27; this could keep compressing margins even as revenue grows.

Open/unresolved items increase near-term uncertainty: the ARC Health ($280k) and Cicada Health ($218.75k) deferred contingent consideration fell due around September 2026 with no independently confirmed settlement found, and the ARC segment's GM transition (Niomi Fleming's departure, effective end-July 2026) lacks a confirmed successor in public sources reviewed — both will need clarification at the H1 FY27 result.

Micro-cap illiquidity and extreme price dispersion persist: third-party data providers show starkly inconsistent and likely stale TAH quotes (ranging roughly NZ$1.6 to over NZ$7 depending on snapshot date) well into FY27, reinforcing the Chairman's own view that market pricing does not reliably track intrinsic value and that the stock is difficult to size meaningfully in a portfolio.
